distribution.title: Chi-squared distribution
distribution.intro: A chi-squared variable with \(\nu\) positive integer degrees of freedom is the sum of squares of \(\nu\) independent standard normal variables. The distribution also extends to positive real degrees of freedom.
distribution.properties: Its mean is \(\nu\), its variance is \(2\nu\), and its support is nonnegative. For a normal sample, \((n-1)S^2/\sigma^2\sim\chi^2_{n-1}\), where \(S^2\) uses denominator \(n-1\).
distribution.course: The course uses the chi-squared distribution to construct a confidence interval for the variance of a normal population.
distribution.course_link: Build a confidence interval for a variance
distribution.r_intro: These examples use functions from R’s stats package. For functions with d, p, q, and r prefixes, they compute a density or mass, cumulative probability, quantile, and random samples, respectively.
distribution.r_code:
dchisq(3, df = 4)
pchisq(3, df = 4)
qchisq(0.95, df = 4)
rchisq(100, df = 4)
